- NEN 9140 Training for Workshop Supervisor English language course: NEN 9140 for Workshop Supervisor For Employers, Health and Safety Officers, and EV Supervisors This e-learning explains the NEN 9140 standard and its implications for working on electric vehicles in the workshop. Essential knowledge for the EV work supervisor, as it answers the question: what exactly are your responsibilities?  Wil je iets vragen? Neem dan contact op met Thomas, onze trainingsspecialist of bel naar 030-6087923 .  Training Information WHY THE NEN 9140 TRAINING FOR WORKSHOP SUPERVISOR In electric vehicles, the propulsion system operates at high voltages. These can pose a danger to people who have to work on these vehicles. The employer is responsible for the safety of the staff. This must ensure a safe workplace and the correct instruction of the staff. For example, an occupational health and safety officer can help with this. The EV workshop supervisor (EV-WV) is the one who is actually in charge of the work on e-vehicles. In this e-learning you will learn what the NEN 9140 standard entails and what the standard regulates for those who work on e-vehicles in the workshop. You can see which employees are allowed to perform certain activities and how the designation policy works. You will learn about personal protective equipment and tools, and the usefulness and necessity of instruction and training. HOW IS THE TRAINING STRUCTURED? The e-learning will be available to you immediately after purchase. The time investment is about 2 hours.

About the project MERIT (MEtabolic Reprogramming in viral pathogenesis: from Infection to Therapeutic innovations) is an EU-funded MSCA training programme aimed at better understanding how viruses affect the human body. Coordinated by Dr. Adithya Sridhar, Assistant Professor, and Prof. Dr. Dasja Pajkrt, Professor of Pediatric Infectious diseases, from the OrganoVIR Labs at Amsterdam UMC (location AMC), this project brings together 7 academic institutions and 12 associated partners from across Europe. Within MERIT, researchers will take a new, holistic approach that focuses on infections and host metabolism to unravel virus-induced metabolic reprogramming and its impact on human health. The project’s objective lies in understanding the complex interplay between viruses and host cells, focusing on metabolic reprogramming, and long-term consequences of infection. This will be achieved by combining three methodological pillars: human organoids, integrative and spatial omics, and advanced microscopy. About the role Despite effective combination antiretroviral therapy (cART), individuals living with HIV experience neurocognitive impairments, collectively known as HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders (HAND). The neuropathological changes observed in HAND are also found in neurodegenerative disorders (NDDs), such as Alzheimer’s disease, Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, and Parkinson’s disease. A common link between HAND and NDDs is disrupted lipid metabolism, with HAND patients exhibiting increased amyloid-beta deposition. Clinical data suggest that TDP-43 proteinopathy may contribute to HAND, further linking it to NDDs. This project aims to explore these connections using iPSC-derived microglia-embedded brain organoids. By characterising lipid profile changes following HIVinfections and investigating TDP-43 proteinopathy, we seek to identify potential mechanisms underlying HAND. At the Amsterdam UMC in the Netherlands, MERIT is looking for a Doctoral Candidate (DC) to work on Work Packages 1 and 2. As DC7, your objectives are: to characterise lipidomic profiles of HIV-infected brain organoids compared to healthy organoids; to assess and alter TDP-43 proteinopathy in HIV-infected organoids. You will be guided during your research project by Prof. Dr. Dasja Pajkrt and Dr. Renata Vieira de Sá at the OrganoVIR Labs at the Amsterdam UMC, Netherlands.
